title: Replication package for "Battery charging, demand statistics and the evaluation of U.S. day-ahead load forecasts"

primary_sources.paraphrase: Dataset record v1.2 (8 Nov 2026, CC-BY-4.0), one author at Shih Chien University: code, data, results and four pre-specification documents for a manuscript said to be submitted to Energy Policy. Audits deteriorating day-ahead load forecasts in EIA-930 for 49 US balancing authorities, 2018-2026. The previewed result file gives CAISO error by year against published load and net of charging.

Changelog. v1.2 recomputes the shares from unrounded yearly values: median share 0.761 (0.765 in v1.0), net median ratio 1.32 (1.31), mean share 0.904 unchanged. Says the manuscript reports 76% (MdAPE), 90% (MAPE), a ratio of 1.32 and a rise of 0.48 points.

The script behind the headline number. Hourly absolute percentage error of CAISO's own day-ahead forecast, January to October, against published load and against load minus charging; yearly median and mean; share of the 2021-to-2026 rise that disappears on the net series. No model is fitted.

File listing of the main archive (contents not readable through the preview): licence, README, about 38 scripts, input archives with SHA-256 manifests, about 80 result files including benchmark re-scoring and weather-adjusted fleet results, and four pre-specification files dated 2026-11-01 in their names.
Version history: 1.0 on 7 Nov 2026, 1.1 and 1.2 on 8 Nov, all with the same zip. The pre-specification documents first became public in the same archive as the results. No linked publication.

claims.text: Netting battery charging out of CAISO's published load removes 76.1% of the rise in the median absolute percentage error of CAISO's day-ahead forecast between 2021 and 2026 (January to October, all hours).
claims.dataset: CAISO published load, day-ahead forecast and battery charging, hourly, Jan-Oct 2021 vs Jan-Oct 2026
claims.baseline: the same forecast scored against published load (charging included)

claims.text: The same calculation on the mean absolute percentage error removes 90.4% of the rise.
claims.dataset: CAISO published load, day-ahead forecast and battery charging, hourly, Jan-Oct 2021 vs Jan-Oct 2026
claims.baseline: the same forecast scored against published load (charging included)

claims.text: Against published load, the median absolute percentage error of CAISO's day-ahead forecast is 3.566% in January to October 2026, up from 1.568% in the same months of 2021.
claims.dataset: CAISO published load and day-ahead forecast, hourly, Jan-Oct 2026

claims.text: Against load net of charging, the median absolute percentage error is 1.975% in January to October 2026, up from 1.498% in 2021 (a rise of 0.48 points).
claims.dataset: CAISO published load minus battery charging, and day-ahead forecast, hourly, Jan-Oct 2026

claims.text: Net of charging, the 2026 median error is still 1.32 times the 2021 value, so part of the deterioration remains.
claims.dataset: CAISO published load minus battery charging, and day-ahead forecast, hourly, Jan-Oct 2021 and 2026

claims.text: Against published load, the mean absolute percentage error is 9.083% in January to October 2026 (2.000% in 2021); net of charging it is 2.551% (1.873% in 2021).
claims.dataset: CAISO published load and day-ahead forecast, hourly, Jan-Oct 2026
claims.baseline: same forecast against load net of charging, Jan-Oct 2026 (2.551)

claims.text: An audit of 49 US balancing authorities in EIA-930 (2018-2026) attributes part of the apparent deterioration of day-ahead load forecasts to how demand is reported, traced case by case against operator series, retail sales and documentation.
claims.dataset: Form EIA-930 BALANCE files, 49 balancing authorities, 2018-2026

relevance.rationale: Hourly electric load from EIA-930, the source of our target series, but at balancing-authority level and centred on CAISO, not PJM zones JC and DOM. The forecasts scored are the operators' own day-ahead forecasts, not a week ahead. No forecasting method is proposed and the inputs of the operators' forecasts are not stated; temperature appears only in a weather adjustment of fleet-level error. The finding is about what the demand series contains, which bears on how EIA-930 demand and any benchmark built on it should be read.

checks.notes: pre_registered: the record lists four pre-specification documents and their file names carry the date 2026-11-01, but they first became public on 7 Nov 2026 inside the same archive as the results, so no public timestamp precedes the results; their contents could not be read through the archive preview. training_overlap_risk: not applicable in substance, there are no pretrained weights and no model is fitted; 'unknown' is used because there is no weights date to compare with the scored window. independent_replication: one search and one research call found no replication, critique, preprint or journal page for this package. A separate public audit (github.com/jinnn11/grid-forecast-audit, commits 28 Oct to 1 Nov 2026, earlier than this package) reaches the same mechanism for CAISO with a different measure: 2025 MAPE falls from 7.31% to 2.45% once charging is taken out of actual load. That agrees in direction but is prior work on another year and metric, not a replication of the 76% share, and whether its author is independent of this one is not stated on either page. It also reports that EIA-930's CAISO demand ran an hour late until 2 Dec 2025; whether the package's CAISO table is affected could not be checked. EIA's own instructions say charging should be left out of demand, with an alternative for respondents that cannot (code DS), so the issue is uneven reporting, not the form's definition. evidence_strength: moderate. Code and result files are public and the headline numbers reproduce arithmetically from the yearly values in the result file (median 1 - 0.477/1.998 = 0.761; mean 1 - 0.678/7.083 = 0.904), the window is far over 90 days and both series use the same forecast and hours; but the headline is descriptive, pre-registration is unverified, nothing is replicated and the manuscript is not public. The share compares two endpoint years (2021 and 2026) and has no interval, so no ci90 is recorded. Central model: none; the forecasts are CAISO's and the other operators' own. Not verified: the 188.9 MB archive was not downloaded, so README, LICENSE, the pre-specification documents, the 49-authority classification files, the benchmark re-scoring and the weather-adjusted fleet results were not read; the first half of the claim (reporting effects across the 49 authorities) rests on the record's description alone. The manuscript and its 'submitted to Energy Policy' status rest on the author's statement. The research answer's statement that no licence is shown is wrong: the Zenodo API gives cc-by-4.0. The CAISO storage report and the scorecard repository were taken from the research tool's sources list and not fetched separately.

label: ACCEPT_STAGE3
label_reason: Sourced and on our target data (hourly EIA-930 demand, with public code and result files that support the three-quarters figure), but it is an audit of operators' own day-ahead forecasts in CAISO, not a forecasting method, so no model in runnable_models can re-measure its headline on PJM zones JC and DOM. What could carry over is a data check on whether our demand series includes storage charging, which is work outside the harness and not a receipt.
implementation_hint: No model from runnable_models is involved; nothing goes through models/chronos2.py or models_ff/run_ff.py. A stage-3 check would be on the data side: look for the EIA-930 storage-demand code (DS) and battery generation for PJM in the BALANCE files, and ask whether the sub-BA demand for JC and DOM counts storage charging, before reading any trend in our errors as a forecasting effect. The package's code/caiso_accuracy_fullhours.py shows the calculation (error against load and against load minus charging); write our own version, the licence of the code inside the archive was not read.
